 Sikkim Supreme enters global markets with exports to US and Australia
 KUNAL RAI
 GANGTOK,: Sikkim Supreme, a well-known local brand of the Government Fruit 
Preservation Factory (GFPF), a Public Sector Undertaking of the Government of 
Sikkim, has made its international debut with its first consignment of products 
being exported to the United States and Australia. 
 Chief Minister 
Prem Singh Tamang-Golay flagged off the first international consignment of 
Sikkim Supreme at a ceremony held at Samman Bhawan gate here on Monday morning. 
The event was attended by Secretary, Commerce and Industries Department, Karma 
D. Youtso, and Managing Director, GFPF, Chanda Rani Rai, among other officials. 
 In a post on 
his official Facebook page, the Chief Minister described the occasion as a 
proud moment for Sikkim, noting that the export initiative would take the State's 
flavours and legacy to the international market. A proud moment for Sikkim as 
Sikkim Supreme goes global, with its first international consignment to the USA 
and Australia, taking the flavours and legacy of Sikkim to the world, he said. 
 He also 
extended his best wishes to the officials and staff of the Commerce and 
Industries Department and GFPF, expressing hope that the milestone would pave 
the way for further global achievements. 
 Speaking to 
the media, Secretary, Commerce and Industries Department, Karma D. Youtso, 
termed the development a historic milestone for the state, as it marks the 
first time that Sikkim Supreme products are entering the international market. 
The initial consignment comprises 12 products for export. 
 Youtso also 
highlighted the department's support through the Raising and Accelerating MSME 
Performance (RAMP) Scheme, under which a 50 per cent subsidy is provided on 
transportation costs for exported goods. She said the department was pleased to 
extend the benefits of the scheme to GFPF and expressed confidence that this 
would mark the beginning of more locally manufactured products reaching 
international markets, bringing recognition and economic opportunities to the 
state. 
 Managing 
Director Chanda Rani Rai expressed her gratitude to the Chief Minister for 
taking the time to flag off the historic consignment. She said the development 
was particularly significant as it coincides with the celebration of 70 years 
of GFPF, which was established in 1956 through the erstwhile Durbar. 
 Describing the 
factory's seven-decade journey as one built on commitment and quality, Rai said 
the international recognition of Sikkim Supreme reflected the standards 
maintained by the institution over the years. She noted that entering the 
global market was not merely a business opportunity but also an affirmation 
that the factory's products meet international quality benchmarks and food 
safety requirements. 
 Rai also 
acknowledged the support extended by the Commerce and Industries Department, 
particularly its initiatives under the RAMP Scheme. She recalled that the 
department had organised a programme titled Sikkim Utsav in Siliguri last year, 
which provided GFPF an opportunity to interact with exporters and explore 
avenues for international trade. The initiative eventually paved the way for 
the present export consignment. 
 Emphasising 
the wider economic significance of the export initiative, Rai said the 
development was not limited to the growth of Sikkim Supreme but represented an 
opportunity for the entire agricultural ecosystem of the state. She pointed out 
that the factory procures its raw materials locally from farmers, adding that 
the brand's expansion into international markets could directly benefit farming 
communities while strengthening the state's agriculture and horticulture 
sectors. 
 She further 
observed that the growth of the brand would have a positive impact on allied 
sectors, including supporting institutions, employment generation and skill 
development, ultimately contributing to rural livelihoods and the overall 
economy of the state. 
 Expressing 
optimism about the future, Rai said GFPF intended to expand its reach in 
international markets while ensuring that the benefits of growth were shared 
across the farming and allied sectors. She reiterated the factory's vision of 
promoting the entire harvest of Sikkim under a unified brand identity, with the 
objective of taking the state's locally produced goods to the global market. 
 The first 
export consignment is destined for New York in the United States and Perth in 
Australia. The consignment to Perth comprises four varieties of pickles: Dalle 
Vinegar, Dalle Bamboo Pickle, Dalle Chilli Pickle and Mixed Pickle. 
 The 
consignment to New York includes 12 products: Dalle Chilli Pickle, Dalle Bamboo 
Pickle, Mixed Pickle, Dalle Vinegar, Dalle Paste, Dalle Chilli Olive Pickle, 
Dalle Bamboo Olive Pickle, Dalle Turmeric Pickle, Passion Squash, Pineapple 
Squash, Kiwi Jam and Mixed Fruit Jam. 
 The diverse 
range of products being exported reflects GFPF's efforts to take multiple 
locally produced varieties to international markets, demonstrating the brand's 
potential to expand beyond individual products while meeting global quality and 
food safety standards.
